questions.question: The play 'Abhijnana Shakuntalam' by Kalidasa is a love story between Shakuntala and King _______.
questions.questionHtml: The play 'Abhijnana Shakuntalam' by Kalidasa is a love story between Shakuntala and King _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Dushyanta.

Key Points

  • Abhigyan Shakuntalam is an excellent drama by Mahakavi Kalidas.
  • It has been acclaimed internationally.
  • It consists of seven acts that deal with the well-known love story of king Dushyant and the maiden Shakuntala.
  • This love story has been presented artistically.
  • It is a pictorial presentation of human feelings.
  • It is an excellent presentation of human love and natural love.

Additional Information

  • Kalidas:
    • He was a Sanskrit author who is often considered ancient India's greatest poet and playwright.
    • His plays and poetry are primarily based on the Vedas, the Mahabharata, and the Purana.
    • He is still remembered because as Kalidas was a writer, he also wrote many moral poems, also the most popular in most of the region.

questions.question: Who is the founder of modern micro finance ?
questions.questionHtml: Who is the founder of modern micro finance ?
questions.solution: Muhammad Yunus is recognized as the founder of modern microfinance, having established the Grameen Bank in Bangladesh in 1983. The bank provides small, collateral-free loans to the impoverished, aiming to empower the poor, especially women, to start small businesses and improve living conditions. Yunus’s model has been replicated globally, aiding millions in escaping poverty. In 2006, he and the Grameen Bank were awarded the Nobel Peace Prize.

    • She was declared as first combat pilot along with two of her cohort Mohana Singh and Avani Chaturvedi.

    • Kanth who hails from Darbhanga, Bihar was born on 1 December 1992.
    • Note: On March 9, 2020, Bhawna Kanth has been awarded Nari Shakti Puraskar by the President of India Ram Nath Kovind.

Additional Information

  • Mohana Singh Jitarwal is one of the first female fighter pilots of India. She was declared as the first female combat pilot along with two of her cohort, Bhawana Kanth, and Avani Chaturvedi.

questions.question: Who among the following classical poets of the Sultanate period in India popularised Qawwali, a form of music which derived its name from the Arabic word ‘qaul’, meaning ‘to speak’?
questions.questionHtml: Who among the following classical poets of the Sultanate period in India popularised Qawwali, a form of music which derived its name from the Arabic word ‘qaul’, meaning ‘to speak’?
questions.solution:
The Correct Answer is Amir Khusrau.

Key Points

  • The famous Sufi saint Hazrat Nizamuddin Olia was the spiritual guru of Amir Khusrau.
  • He was a great musician, scholar, and poet.
  • Amir Khusrau is considered to be the first poet of Khadi Boli Hindi and Urdu.
  • Tabla, Sitar, and Qawwali were invented by Amir Khusro.
  • Kiran-us-Saden, Mifta-ul-Futuh, Khazain-ul-Futuh, Ashika, and Tughlaqnama are his main books.
  • Amir Khusrau was famous as the parrot of Hind.
  • His creations are a reflection of Indian social culture not only at the level of sensitivity but also at the level of craft
  • His real name was Abul Hasan Yaminuddin Muhammad.
  • Amir Khusro was born in 1253 AD in a town named Patiali in Etah (Uttar Pradesh). 
  • He was given the title of Khusro at the age of just 12 by the scholar Khwaja Ijuddin.
  • His spiritual guru's name was Nizamuddin Olia, who was famous as Mehboob-e-Ilahi.
  • His Guru Nizamuddin Olia had seen the period of 7 Sultans in Delhi.

Additional Information

  • Nizam al-Din Awliya - 
    • Like most of the Chishti Sufi saints, Nizamuddin Auliya stressed love as a means of realising God.
    • He believed the love of God implied a love of humanity.
    • He had a major influence on the Muslims of Delhi and the world over.
  • Jalal al-Din Muhammad Rumi - 
    • Rūmī was a great Sufi mystic and poet in the Persian language, famous for his lyrics and for his didactic epic Mas̄navī-yi Maʿnavī (“Spiritual Couplets”), which widely influenced mystical thought and literature throughout the Muslim world.​
  • Shams al-Din Muhammad Hafiz - 
    • Hafez of Shiraz (also given as Hafiz, l. 1315-1390) is considered the greatest of the Persian poets and among the most famous and admired writers in world literature.
    • He is among the most often translated poets in the present day and his work continues to resonate with modern audiences.

questions.question: TH Vinayakram is associated with which musical instrument?
questions.questionHtml: TH Vinayakram is associated with which musical instrument?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is ghatam.

Key Points

  • Thetakudi Harihara Vinayakram, also known as Vikku Vinayakram, is an Indian percussionist.
  • He is also known as the God of ghatam.
  • He plays Carnatic music with the ghatam, an earthen pot, and is credited with popularising the ghatam.
  • Ghatam is a large, narrow-mouthed earthenware water pot used as a percussion instrument in India. Unlike other Indian percussion instruments, such as the tabla and mridangam, the ghatam does not have a membrane over its mouth.

Additional Information

  • The dholak is a two-headed hand drum, a folk percussion instrument. The instrument is about 45 cm in length and 27 cm in breadth and is widely used in qawwali, kirtan, lavani, and bhangra. The drum has two different-sized drumheads.
  • The sarod is a stringed instrument, used mainly in Hindustani music on the Indian subcontinent. Along with the sitar, it is among the most popular and prominent instruments.
  • A tabla is a pair of twin-hand drums from the Indian subcontinent. Since the 18th century, it has been the principal percussion instrument in Hindustani classical music.

questions.question: Who among the following was well - known for their kathakali dancing?
questions.questionHtml: Who among the following was well - known for their kathakali dancing?
questions.solution: Madavoor Vasudevan Nair was a renowned Kathakali artist from Kerala, India, known for his mastery of Kathi (villainous) and Pacha (heroic) roles in this classical dance-drama form. questions.question: Anna Chandy, the first Indian woman to serve as a judge at a high court was appointed in which High Court?
questions.questionHtml: Anna Chandy, the first Indian woman to serve as a judge at a high court was appointed in which High Court?
questions.solution: Anna Chandy was the first Indian woman to serve as a judge at a high court, appointed to the Kerala High Court. Her tenure lasted from 9 February 1959 to 5 April 1967. She was also one of the first female judges in the Commonwealth countries. Her appointment was a significant milestone in the Indian judiciary, representing a major step forward for women's representation in the legal profession. Anna Chandy's contributions to the judiciary were profound, and she passed away in 1996.

questions.question: Who among the following assassinated Sir William Hutt Curzon Wyllie in London?
questions.questionHtml: Who among the following assassinated Sir William Hutt Curzon Wyllie in London?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Madan Lal Dhingra.

Key Points

  • On 1 July 1909, in London Curzon Wyllie was assassinated by the Indian revolutionary Madan Lal Dhingra, who was a member of India House in London
  • Sir William Hutt Curzon Wyllie was a British Indian army officer.
  • Madan Lal Dhingra claimed that he had murdered Curzon-Wyllie as a patriotic act and in revenge for the inhumane killings of Indians by the British Government in India.
  • When Curzon Wyllie, political aide-de-camp to the Secretary of State for India, was leaving the hall with his wife, Dhingra fired five shots right at his face, four of which hit their target.
  • He was found guilty and sentenced to death. He was executed at Pentonville Prison on 17 August 1909.

Additional Information

  • ​Madan Lal Dhingra was born on 18 February 1883 in Amritsar, India, and died on 17 August 1909.
  • He was an Indian revolutionary, pro-independence activist, while studying in England, he assassinated William Hutt Curzon Wyllie.
  • Curzon Wylie had joined the British Army in 1866 and the Indian Political Department in 1879. In 1901, he was selected to be Political Aide-de-Camp to the Secretary of State for India.
  • He was also the head of the Secret Police and had been trying to obtain information about Savarkar and his fellow revolutionaries.
  • On the evening of 1 July 1909, Madan Lal Dhingra, along with a large number of Indians and Englishmen had gathered to attend the annual 'At Home' function hosted by the Indian National Association at the Imperial Institute. 
    • When Curzon Wyllie, political aide-de-camp to the Secretary of State for India, was leaving the hall with his wife, Dhingra fired five shots right at his face, four of which hit their target. a Parsee doctor Cawas Lalcaca tried to save Curzon Wyllie died of Dhingra's sixth and seventh bullets.
